title: Lynkk vs Otter.ai Comparison: Otter AI Alternative, Feature by Feature (2026) | Lynkk

lines: Your meeting ran an hour.
On Otter's free plan, a conversation stops at 30 minutes.
Here's how Lynkk and Otter.ai compare, feature by feature, as of October 2026.
First, recording.
Both tools can send a bot to Zoom, Google Meet and Teams, and both can record without one.
Lynkk gives you four ways: the Mac app, the Chrome extension, the meeting bot, and your mic in the browser for meetings in person.
On the Mac and in Chrome, nothing joins the call.
The Mac app notices calls in Zoom, Meet, Teams, Slack huddles, WhatsApp, FaceTime and Webex, and asks if you want to record.
It records both sides on two channels, so the transcript labels your lines You.
When the call ends, it stops by itself.
Languages.
Otter lists six: English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese and Chinese, one language per conversation.
Lynkk transcribes 17, with auto-detect. That includes Hindi, Arabic, Korean and Portuguese, with Tamil, Telugu, Marathi and Bengali in beta.
Long meetings.
On Otter's free plan, a conversation stops at 30 minutes. On Pro, it stops at 90.
Lynkk records up to 2 hours per recording, on every plan, the free plan included.
After the call, Lynkk writes a Meeting Brief.
Key takeaways with timestamps, decisions, open questions, and action items with an owner, a due date and a priority.
Every timestamp plays the recording from that moment. The Meeting Brief is on the free plan.
Every action item lands on one task board, across all your meetings.
From the note, send them to Jira, one issue per item. You pick the project and the issue type.
On Pro, Ask Lynkk answers only from your own notes.
You ask in plain words, and the answer carries citation chips.
Play from takes you to the moment it was said.

scenes.chapter: Before the call, and in Slack
lines: With Google Calendar connected, Lynkk emails you a morning briefing on days you have meetings.
Who you're meeting, the last note with them, and how many action items are still open between you.
On Pro, ask @Lynkk in a Slack channel, and it answers in the thread from your own notes, with sources.
To be fair, Otter is the better pick for some teams.
It has a Windows app, it transcribes files you upload, and its AI chat across meetings is on every plan.
Its Enterprise plan lists SSO and SCIM for large companies.
Lynkk's app is Mac only, it transcribes what it records, Ask Lynkk is part of Pro, and a workspace has up to 10 seats.
So, the short version.
Pick Lynkk if your calls run in more languages than Otter's six, if your meetings run past 30 minutes, or if you want nothing joining the call on your Mac.
And Lynkk never trains on your conversations.
Lynkk records the call, writes the brief, and hands your tasks to Jira.
Start free at lynkk.ai.
